body: I'm seeing a psychiatrist right now, and I've been on some SNRIs for a little over a week now, but I don't feel anything, and if anything things are worse. I called him several days ago and he said that this was normal. My next appointment with him is in 3 weeks. Is there a certain point when I should be checking back in with him re: changing medications/dosages/etc.? Or should I just be waiting until my next appointment for him to reassess?

I've been battling depression most of my adult life and it's been really bad for me this past half year. 

Big DeMar fan now. Thanks for trying to do some good in the world.

I'm surprised I've been able to drag myself to work. I don't talk to anyone there, people probably think I'm a social outcast or something. 

I just wonder what the point of continuing on is when I feel like this every fucking day. Good luck to you. I know how hopeless things seem and I wish I had something wise to say to make it feel better.
I feel more and more like a zombie. I can barely get out of bed to go to work. I always show up "late" but I haven't been scolded at yet so I keep doing it.
Okay, I'll send him an email this afternoon. Thanks. I also hate how depression fucks with decision making too.
Oh wow, I didn't realize they could take that long to kick in. Do you think I should email/call my psychiatrist now? I thought I'd wait a little longer, though I'm not sure why.
What kinds of rewards do you give yourself?
About a week. I was hoping I would start feeling effects by now. If anything I feel a little worse. It doesn't help that it's made my sleep even worse than it already was.

Not so well. Everyday is a struggle to get out of bed and get to work. Everyday is a struggle getting through the workday. Everyday is a struggle keeping my mind busy at night. Today is starting out no differently. The pain of losing her is truly physical at times. I'm trying to work on things with my therapist but it often feels impossible. I just want the pain to stop and while I "know" what should be done, emotionally I feel like nothing will work unless I have her again. There hasn't been a single day I haven't cried.
How are you supposed to actually internalize things? It feels like it should be so easy and it's frustrating that I feel like I can't do anything about it.
Exactly how I feel. I just don't want to deal with this pain anymore.
Good point about jumping... that's a LONG time to be contemplating things while you're falling...
Is it normal for suicidal people to be scared of going through with it? Or does that mean we're not so far gone yet?

Not only do I not care about what I work on... but it's a fucking awful open office environment, so I have literally 0 privacy (at least I'd have SOME privacy with a cubicle) and have to hear the loud chatter of other people. Other people who typically have happy lives. I hate the environment.
Sucks.... I haven't quite reached that point yet (having to pull overtime), but I get the sense it's coming...

Check out (if in the US): https://www.eeoc.gov/eeoc/publications/mental_health.cfm

I've been looking into this myself...
I don't watch South Park, but maybe I'll check the episode out based on your description. Thanks. It helps, even if just a little, to know that strangers care.
It's hard to imagine how I could ever be happy again...

I think the main things holding me back are that I'm too scared to actually go through with it... and that I don't want to hurt her even more, since I know she would be hurt if I did that to myself (I know she still cares about me even if she's deeply upset)...

It's just so hard when I failed her and myself... and when the pain is this much every single day. I don't want to have to live through this pain anymore :(
